name: Bosnia and Herzegovina

observations.reasoning: DISPUTED. Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. 3531159 inhabitants, the 2013 census figure, read on the front page of the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which displays it as Populacija 2013. Eurostat carries a geo code for the country but publishes no row for it at all in demo_pjan, which is why the national agency was opened instead. Status disputed on the age of the figure: thirteen years, and a census rather than an estimate, in a country whose population is widely held to have fallen substantially since through emigration. Using it as a denominator for a per-inhabitant indicator would understate the rate by whatever that fall amounts to. The agency publishes annual estimates that were not reached from the front page in this pass; they are the thing to fetch.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Bosnian and Croatian, in the transversal venues pass. Three units, two houses and one stage. The opening estimate was 2.5 and named Mostar, Sarajevo and Banja Luka; it lands near the right number by getting two of those three cities wrong and by missing that Mostar holds two puppet theatres rather than one. The candidate list did not come from a ministry — culture in Bosnia and Herzegovina is an entity and cantonal competence and no register spans the country — but from the national puppet festival, the Susret pozorišta/kazališta lutaka BiH, held in Bugojno since 1979 and the oldest in the country. Its organiser, the public KSC Bugojno, names the theatres that come: Dječije pozorište Republike Srpske in Banja Luka, Pozorište lutaka Mostar, Lutkarsko kazalište Mostar, Bosansko narodno pozorište Zenica, Pozorište mladih Sarajevo, and its own Eko Art Bugojno. Six candidates, each then read on its own pages, and only three survive the denominator. Mostar carries two, and the war is the reason: the Gradsko pozorište lutaka founded in 1952 has two successors on either side of the city, both of them on the City of Mostar's own list of gradske ustanove with their addresses and telephone numbers, so both are city institutions and neither is a programming strand. Pozorište lutaka Mostar plays in the former synagogue in Braće Ćišića; Lutkarsko kazalište Mostar plays on Trg hrvatskih velikana and lists its own ansambl. Both are houses whose vocation is puppetry and both count, which is what the denominator says and not a comment on the division. The stage is Zenica. Javna ustanova Bosansko narodno pozorište Zenica, financed by the Zeničko-dobojski kanton and founded by the Grad Zenica, carries a named permanent unit since 1951, the Dječija, omladinska i lutkarska scena, which has its own head, its own site at dols.bnp.ba and its own line in the parent's structure. It produces puppetry now, not historically: its Prodani smijeh opened the 23rd Susret and took a prize for puppet animation, and BNP played the puppet production Grad svjetlosti in Mostar on 2 July 2026. This is the weakest of the three and the reason the observation is disputed. The scene is not exclusively a puppet unit — it is children's, youth and puppet in one, and the word lutkarska entered its name only in 2004/05 — and it shows no puppeteers of its own, distinct from the acting ensemble of the house. It is counted because the ruling counts a named stage inside a larger organisation, and this one is named, permanent and currently producing. Someone applying the same ruling could refuse it. Three fall out on vocation, on the line Kolibri settled. Pozorište mladih Sarajevo is the sharpest loss and the one that will look wrong: it is the direct successor of the Sarajevo Pozorište lutaka of 1950, which Adolf Pomezny built on marionettes and Jurislav Korenić developed, and it plays at the puppet festival. But that puppet theatre was merged into the Pionirsko pozorište in 1977, and what came out has one company. Its own site lists a single kolektiv with no puppet scene, no puppet ensemble and no puppet department, and the Canton Sarajevo ministry page for the institution names none either. A theatre descended from a puppet theatre is not a puppet unit. Dječije pozorište Republike Srpske goes the same way and it costs more: it holds the only museum of theatre puppets in southeastern Europe, five hundred of them from its own productions, and it has run an international children's theatre festival since 2002. Its ansambl page still shows one company of sixteen actors, described one by one, with a single member noted for puppetry. A museum is an archive of a practice, not a permanent unit of it. JU Pozorište Prijedor, fully financed by the city, took two prizes at the last Susret and names no puppet unit on its own pages or on the city's. Eko Art Bugojno is the festival organiser's own children's theatre, playing with its mentors and young performers, so it is not a professional permanent ensemble. Three is a floor and a narrow one. Nothing here was read in a register, only on the institutions' own pages and their founders'; the entity-level ministries were not reached and the strict test — does a permanent puppetry unit exist inside this house — is exactly the one an institutional website is least reliable about. Prijedor and Banja Luka are the two that would move first if their staff lists were read.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. The Academy of Performing Arts of the University of Sarajevo, the main public institution in the field, was checked department by department: acting opened in 1981, directing in 1989, dramaturgy in 1994, production and management in 2010, audiovisual arts in 2016. No puppetry department. The country does have institutional puppetry activity, the Mostar puppet theatre running an international festival of the form, but production is not training and does not stand in for it in this indicator. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1: the arts academy of Banja Luka was not checked. Estimate, resting on search summaries.
